slides.title: Aid in Tigray nearly stopped
slides.body: What The New Humanitarian reported, October 2026
Mekelle was cut off from the outside world, and aid operations largely halted, with no telecom, fuel or cash

slides.title: A food convoy was struck
slides.body: Aid transport was judged too risky after a drone strike hit a convoy in the northwest. The federal government did not acknowledge the attack.
people in need receive no food assistance, as distribution now targets only displaced people after donor cuts
displaced people in 31 camps are served by one aid group, OSSHD-Ethiopia, which says looting cost it its vehicles and equipment and has paused its work

slides.title: One route could matter
slides.body: The 460 km Mekelle–Semera corridor was reported functional on Oct 4 and could allow a surge in aid if it stays safe.

slides.title: Protect aid workers. Restore communications. Allow safe humanitarian access.
slides.body: Follow for sourced updates from across Ethiopia.

source: Source: The New Humanitarian, "Tigray faces a double catastrophe" · Oct 8, 2026

card.title: Aid nearly stopped
card.body: Mekelle was cut off and aid largely halted, reports The New Humanitarian.
